subject: Request: cash-collar & deferred liquidated damages for high-availability tiers
messages:
From: Elaine Chu <elaine.chu@medsys.org>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, procurement@medsys.org
Cc: Tom Ryder <tom.ryder@medsys.org>
Date: 2026-06-25T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: MedSys SLA remedies request (redlines attached)

Priyom / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the productive demo last week. Attached is a focused ask from our legal and ops teams (MedSys_Requested_SLA_Remedies_20260625.pdf) — we need written commitments that go beyond service credits for the high-availability tier we expect to purchase. High level:

- Immediate fee-at-risk: a cash-collar (escrow) covering at least 3 months of committed fees to be drawn down in serious outages.
- Liquidated damages language for repeat P1/P2 events (we provided sample wording in the PDF).
- A unilateral termination right for MedSys if cumulative unavailability exceeds X% or if there are 3 unrecovered P1s in a 60-day window.
- Short cure periods (30 days) and limited opportunity for multiple retries.

We appreciate Redwood's standard credits approach, but for our regulated workflows we need enforceable financial remedies and termination to satisfy our audit/compliance board. Please review and come back with your position and any alternative constructs you can accept by EOD PDT next Thursday (7/1).

Also please include SOC2 evidence (summary fine). I've attached our requested redlines and the sample legal text. Happy to set a 30-min call to walk through.

Thanks,
Elaine Chu
Senior Procurement Manager, MedSys Health
elaine.chu@medsys.org
+1 415 555 0189

Attachments: MedSys_Requested_SLA_Remedies_20260625.pdf
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Chu <elaine.chu@medsys.org>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-25T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MedSys SLA remedies request (redlines attached)

Elaine — thanks for the clear ask and the redlines. We understand the compliance drivers and respect the need for stronger financial remedies in regulated contracts. I’ll coordinate with Legal and Ops as a priority.

High level response up front:
- We’re open to a staged cash-collar (escrow) tied to committed spend but need to cap exposure and define triggers precisely.
- We cannot accept broad liquidated-damages language without narrow definitions of severity and causation; Redwood’s preference is tiered remedies (credits + capped holdback) rather than open-ended LDs.
- Termination for repeated severity P1s is feasible with agreed cure windows and an objective escalation matrix.

I’ll propose specific contract language after internal alignment. Can we schedule a 30-min call next Tuesday (6/30) to review our counterproposal live? I’ve looped in Marissa (sales lead) and Ben (pricing/finance) to expedite.

– Priyom
Priyom Das
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai | +1 650 555 0122
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-25T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: MedSys SLA remedies request — internal notes

Team — quick internal read: Elaine is asking for remedies that materially increase financial exposure. A few pointers before we draft language:

- Push back on any undefined LD trigger. We should require an objective incident taxonomy (P1 = service-wide outage affecting >X% of routed requests or sustained latency >Y ms for Z min).
- Prefer an escrow-style reserve funded quarterly up to an agreed cap (example: max 3 months of committed fees initial; 6 months as a step-up only if repeat breaches occur across multiple quarters).
- Cure periods: accept 30 days for operational fixes, but require an attempt/cure definition and an opportunity for remediation before termination.
- No open-ended unilateral termination; termination should be available after multiple unremediated breaches with a cure window and an ability to arbitrate or use a third-party auditor to validate.

Ben — get me a quick model of what 3 vs 6 month caps look like for their anticipated commit (attach model). Vanessa — can you confirm whether Private deployment (VPC) is a gating control they could adopt to reduce remedies?

Marissa
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Chu <elaine.chu@medsys.org>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-26T09:44:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood counterproposal — staged reserve + objective triggers (redlines attached)

Elaine — following internal alignment, please find a summarized counterproposal below. Full redlines are attached (MedSys_Redlines_0625.docx) and we’ve also included a SOC2 summary for your reviewers (SOC2_Type2_Summary.pdf).

Summary of Redwood counterproposal:
1) Staged cash-collar (escrow): Redwood will place a reserve funded at contract start equivalent to 3 months of committed fees (drawn only for validated severe incidents). The reserve increases to a 6-month cap only if there are 2 independent incident windows meeting the P1 definition within any rolling 12-month period.

2) Objective incident definitions & validation: P1/P2 definitions will be mutually agreed and tied to quantifiable availability and latency metrics. A third-party technical validation (jointly appointed) will adjudicate contested incidents.

3) Cure and remediation: Customer will provide written notice; Redwood will have a 30-day remediation period. If Redwood fails to remediate within that window for a validated P1, MedSys may draw on the reserve up to the per-incident cap.

4) Termination: MedSys may terminate only after 3 validated, unrecovered P1s within a 90-day window OR 4 validated P1s within 12 months. Termination will require notice and the standard wind-down period to protect live traffic.

5) No open-ended liquidated damages: Redwood cannot accept uncapped LDs; the reserve model provides predictable financial exposure while preserving operational continuity.

We believe this construct balances audit/compliance needs with predictable vendor risk. If MedSys requires alternative language for immediate fee-at-risk, we can consider a short-term pilot (higher reserve) where terms are revisited after Q1.

Available for a 30-min call tomorrow (6/27) or Tue (6/30).

Best,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai | +1 650 555 0122

Attachments: MedSys_Redlines_0625.docx, SOC2_Type2_Summary.pdf
From: Tom Ryder <tom.ryder@medsys.org>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elaine Chu <elaine.chu@medsys.org>, procurement@medsys.org
Date: 2026-06-29T10:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood counterproposal — staged reserve + objective triggers

Priyom — thanks for the quick counterproposal. A few notes from our legal team:

- The staged reserve is a good start, but our counsel is pressing for an express fee-at-risk that is immediately available for P1s without multi-step adjudication.
- They’re also asking for a shorter remediation window for mission-critical workflows (15 days) and a clause that allows MedSys to terminate for cause after two unrecovered P1s in a 60-day window.

We don’t want to stall procurement — can Redwood provide written language that makes the reserve immediately available for validated P1s (without requiring the 3-P1/90-day threshold to draw down)? We can live with a higher cap if so. If Redwood is unwilling, we’ll need to escalate internally to get approval to move forward.

Please advise — if you can provide explicit contract text we can run with legal, that helps a lot.

— Tom
Tom Ryder
Head of IT Operations | MedSys Health
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ryder <tom.ryder@medsys.org>, Elaine Chu <elaine.chu@medsys.org>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-29T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood counterproposal — staging an exec decision and limited immediate drawdown option

Tom / Elaine — thank you. I’ve escalated to Marissa and Vanessa for an exec OK on one-time concessions we can make to close the deal without exposing Redwood to uncapped liability. Proposed path: 

1) Immediate drawdown option: Redwood will permit immediate drawdown from the reserve for a validated P1 up to a per-incident cap equal to 25% of the monthly committed fee, subject to a post-incident validation step (technical review within 10 business days). This provides money-up-front while preserving objective validation.

2) Remediation window: we can reduce the operational remediation window to 21 days for mission-critical endpoints (not platform-wide) with a clear scoping definition. We cannot accept a blanket 15-day cure across all services.

3) Termination: Redwood can accept accelerated termination for two unrecovered P1s in a 60-day window only if MedSys agrees to an expedited arbitration path to resolve causation disputes (to prevent wrongful termination).

If MedSys accepts the above, Redwood will produce explicit contract text and a DocuSign-ready redline by end of day Thursday. We will also provide a one-off finance-approved reserve model (4 weeks of committed fees) as a compromise on cap if you sign within 30 days.

Please let me know if that path is acceptable — happy to take this to an exec-to-exec call Thursday morning.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
